title: How Much of a Snowsports School Block Had Been Taught When a Session Was Lost
content:
The share of the session value that is made good on a Snowsports School booking turns on how much of the block the school had already taught when the session was lost, counted as the delivery entries standing on the booking's school account.

## The ladder of shares

| Sessions of the block already delivered when the session was lost | Share of the session value made good |
| --- | --- |
| 3 or more | 100 percent |
| 1 or 2 | 80 percent |
| none | 50 percent |

Where three or more of the block's sessions had already been delivered, the late block share of 100 percent is made good. Where one or two of them had been delivered, the mid block share of 80 percent is made good. Where none of them had been delivered, the share stands at 50 percent.

## What is counted

The count is of the delivery entries standing on that booking's school account — one entry for each session delivered to the participant — taken as they stand on the handling date. Sessions still to come are not counted, and entries standing on another booking of the same household account are not counted.

## Both sides of each threshold

- A booking on whose account 2 delivery entries stand falls in the middle band, at 80 percent; a third delivery entry moves it to 100 percent.
- A booking on whose account no delivery entry stands falls at 50 percent; a single delivery entry moves it to 80 percent.
- A booking on whose account 5 delivery entries stand is above the upper threshold and sits at 100 percent, as does one on whose account exactly 3 stand.

## A reading on hypothetical figures

Take a session value of 300.00 USD on a Snowsports School booking. Where no session of the block had yet been delivered, 50 percent of that value is 150.00 USD. Where two sessions had been delivered, 80 percent of it is 240.00 USD. Where four had been delivered, the whole 300.00 USD is made good.
